data.one_liner: Create two-component states with an isolated backend part and a frontend part for UI-isolates.
data.what_it_does: Isolator splits state logic into a Frontend component that runs in the UI thread and a Backend component that runs in a separate isolate. It enables communication between them to handle CPU-heavy computations or big-data parsing without dropping UI frames. It also supports interactors for communication between different backends.
use_when: You have heavy CPU-bound tasks or data parsing that causes jank in the UI isolate
You want to organize state into isolated backend components and frontend UI components
avoid_when: Your application is simple and state management can be handled on a single thread without performance issues
You are targeting platforms where isolates have limitations or you prefer standard single-threaded state managers
strengths: Keeps the UI thread unblocked for smooth 60/120 fps animations
Provides a structured way to run business logic in background isolates without complex boilerplate
weaknesses: Adds architectural complexity with split Frontend and Backend components
Does not provide true multi-threading on Flutter Web due to platform limitations
data.setup_notes: Requires structuring state into paired Frontend and Backend components rather than standard single-class state management.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want standard single-threaded reactive state management with extensive community plugins and widgets.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a compile-safe, modern provider-based state management solution without managing isolates manually.
